nodes.title: Use WS_EX_NOREDIRECTIONBITMAP to reduce memory usage when creating Windows in Microsoft Windows
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a feature request that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Problem Description

The Windows windowing system was built with GDI, so it creates a default GDI canvas for every window. This canvas uses 3 bytes per pixel, about 6 MB for a 1080p screen. For self-rendering apps like Electron, this canvas is unnecessary. Since the memory is not allocated by the application itself but by the DWM, there is no simple way to accurately measure and test it. The only way to disable it is to pass WS_EX_NOREDIRECTIONBITMAP to CreateWindowEx. Electron Apps should use this optimization.

Background:
https://github.com/microsoft/terminal/pull/20655
https://github.com/microsoft/microsoft-ui-xaml/issues/11523

### Proposed Solution

Update the document native-code-and-electron-cpp-win32.md

### Alternatives Considered

none

### Additional Information

_No response_

`native-code-and-electron-cpp-win32.md` is a _simple_ code example not intended to be used as a copy-paste production code sample.

Your automated code search across github did not understand the context before making this issue 😅 

All _actual_ windows Electron makes already have `WS_EX_NOREDIRECTIONBITMAP` (inherited via Chromium)

nodes.title: svg filters on webview stopped working
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

44.0.0-alpha.1

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Other (specify below)

### Operating System Version

confirmed on all three platforms

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

43.x

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

No

### Expected Behavior

When applying an SVG filter through CSS, the filter should be applied. This is what happens in Electron 43

### Actual Behavior

Starting from electron 44, the SVG filter is no longer applied (however CSS filters still are)

### Testcase Gist URL

https://gist.github.com/Kilian/c0d1f460e23a80106f7cce41c9bae325

### Additional Information

Open the testcase and see the difference between 43.x and 44.x. In 44.x the SVG filter is correctly applied to the div but not to the webview. It is applied to both in 43.x

This bug starts right at the first 44 alpha, so i don't know when the specific change was made.

> This bug starts right at the first 44 alpha, so i don't know when the specific change was made.

Could you check the v44 nightly versions? (You might have to enable nightly versions in the Fiddle settings first.)

The first broken build is `44.0.0-nightly-20260612` with `44.0.0-nightly-20260610` being the last working one: https://github.com/electron/electron/compare/v44.0.0-nightly.20260610...v44.0.0-nightly.20260612

This is intentional upstream behavior rather than something we broke. Chromium stopped painting SVG reference filters (`filter: url(#...)`) on cross-origin frames in M151 in response to https://lyra.horse/blog/2025/12/svg-clickjacking/ (https://crbug.com/476646486). A `<webview>` guest is composited as a remote frame in the embedder so it falls under the same rule. CSS filter functions like `grayscale()` aren't affected, which lines up with what you're seeing.

Chrome does the same thing, your testcase just doesn't hit it there because the `<div>` isn't a frame. Put `filter: url(#greyscale)` on a cross-origin `<iframe>` in Chrome and it's ignored too. The `PreventSvgFilterPaint` feature flag was removed in M152 so there's no `--disable-features` escape hatch on 44, and patching the restriction back out would reopen the hole it closes.

The restriction only applies to filters the embedder puts on the frame, so the workaround is to apply the filter from inside the guest. Tested this on 45 and main:

```js
const svg = `<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><filter id="f" color-interpolation-filters="linearRGB"><feColorMatrix type="matrix" values="0.299 0.587 0.114 0 0 0.299 0.587 0.114 0 0 0.299 0.587 0.114 0 0 0 0 0 1 0"/></filter></svg>`

webview.addEventListener('dom-ready', () => {
  webview.insertCSS(`html { filter: url("data:image/svg+xml,${encodeURIComponent(svg)}#f") !important; }`)
})
```

One catch: cross-origin iframes _inside_ the guest page hit the same restriction one level down, so embedded content (videos, ads, etc.) renders unfiltered. You'd probably have to inject into each subframe as well (`frame.executeJavaScript` over `webContents.mainFrame.framesInSubtree`), haven't tried that though.

Going to close this out since it's working as intended in Chromium.
fair enough, thanks for looking into it!

### Electron Version

44.2.0

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Windows

### Operating System Version

Windows 10 22H2 and Windows 11 25H2

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

43.X.X

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

No

### Expected Behavior

`app.commandLine.appendSwitch('enable-features', 'OverlayScrollbar')` called before `app.whenReady()` should enable overlay scrollbars for all windows, as it did in Electron 43.x

### Actual Behavior

After upgrading to Electron 44.x, all windows still render classic scrollbars.

`app.commandLine.getSwitchValue('enable-features')` returns `OverlayScrollbar`, so the switch itself is set correctly, but it has no effect.

### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_

### Additional Information

You can use an AI coding assistant and simply ask it to enable the overlay scrollbar in Electron.

This is an unsupported Chromium flag, not part of API.

It recently changed in Chromium, the new syntax is:

```
--enable-features=OverlayScrollbar:mode/classic
--enable-features=OverlayScrollbar:mode/device (follows OS preference)
--enable-features=OverlayScrollbar:mode/overlay
```

nodes.title: [Bug]: new BrowserWindow() never returns under --ozone-platform=headless, then the process segfaults
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

40.10.2

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Linux

### Operating System Version

Arch Linux, kernel 7.2.3-arch1-2, Wayland session (also reproduces with the display environment variables unset)

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

Not determined — only 40.10.2 was available to test on this machine.

### Expected Behavior

With `--ozone-platform=headless`, `new BrowserWindow()` should return and the window should load, as it does under `--headless=new`, `--ozone-platform=x11`, and `--ozone-platform=wayland`.

### Actual Behavior

Under `--ozone-platform=headless`, `app.whenReady()` resolves normally but **`new BrowserWindow()` never returns**. The constructor blocks for roughly 60 seconds, then the process dies with SIGSEGV. No window is ever created and no renderer is spawned.

Instrumenting the main process shows exactly where it stops:

```
# --ozone-platform=headless --disable-gpu --no-sandbox
+0ms   start
+14ms  whenReady resolved
        <- hangs here ~60s, then SIGSEGV (exit 139, core dumped)

# --headless=new --disable-gpu --no-sandbox
+0ms   start
+56ms  whenReady resolved
+74ms  BrowserWindow constructed
+133ms did-finish-load
+134ms quit 0
```

Reproduces independently of GPU and sandbox flags:

| flags | result |
|---|---|
| `--ozone-platform=headless --disable-gpu --no-sandbox` | hang → SIGSEGV |
| `--ozone-platform=headless --no-sandbox` | hang → SIGSEGV |
| `--ozone-platform=headless` (sandbox on, GPU on) | hang → SIGSEGV |
| `--headless=new --disable-gpu --no-sandbox` | works, exit 0 |
| `--ozone-platform=x11 --disable-gpu --no-sandbox` | works, exit 0 |
| `--ozone-platform=wayland --disable-gpu --no-sandbox` | works, exit 0 |

Possibly relevant: in the runs where the GPU is not disabled, the headless process still emits an **X11/GLX** error before dying, which is unexpected for a platform that should not be talking to X at all:

```
X Error of failed request:  BadMatch (invalid parameter attributes)
  Major opcode of failed request:  150 (GLX)
  Minor opcode of failed request:  5 (X_GLXMakeCurrent)
```

The core dump's crashing thread could not be symbolized (no debug symbols for the release binary), so I can only report the observable behavior, not the faulting frame.

### Testcase Gist URL

https://gist.github.com/Zeus-Deus/1797bbc852e232e83501db1b35f294a4

### Additional Information

Full reproduction — a `package.json` with `"main": "main.js"` plus the gist file:

```bash
electron . --ozone-platform=headless --disable-gpu --no-sandbox --user-data-dir=/tmp/ud-a   # hang, then SIGSEGV
electron . --headless=new            --disable-gpu --no-sandbox --user-data-dir=/tmp/ud-b   # works
```

Impact: `--ozone-platform=headless` is a common way to run Electron apps in
automated/CI-style environments without a display server. On this version it
fails in a way that is easy to misread — the app dumps core on every launch,
which on desktops that surface core dumps looks like an application crash
rather than an unsupported flag. `--headless=new` is a working substitute.

GPU subprocess crash (STATUS_BREAKPOINT / exit_code=-2147483645) on Intel Iris Xe Tiger Lake
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

43.5.0

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Windows

### Operating System Version

Shipped with Signal Desktop 8.26.0 (Electron 32.x range)

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

Unknown

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

I don't know how to test

### Expected Behavior

Signal Desktop (and other Electron apps) should start normally with a visible window and working renderer.

### Actual Behavior

Signal silently crashes at startup with no window shown. The GPU subprocess exits with `STATUS_BREAKPOINT` (`0x80000003` / exit code `-2147483645`). This is a related but distinct variant from the original reports in #32440 which showed `STATUS_ACCESS_VIOLATION` (`0xC0000005`).

Windows Application Event Log (Event ID 1000):
```text
Faulting application: Signal.exe
Exception code: 0x80000003 (STATUS_BREAKPOINT)
Fault offset: 0x0000000006fefb69  ← identical across every crash attempt
```

Running with `--disable-gpu` surfaces the GPU subprocess crash explicitly:
```text
[ERROR:gpu_process_host.cc:1108] GPU process exited unexpectedly: exit_code=-2147483645
[FATAL:gpu_data_manager_impl_private.cc:416] GPU process isn't usable. Goodbye.
```

**Secondary issue:** Even after working around the startup crash with `--in-process-gpu`, newly spawned renderer processes (e.g. Help → About window) crash with the same exit code:
```text
Render process is gone
Error: Reason: crashed, Exit Code: -2147483645
```

### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_

### Additional Information

### Hardware
- GPU: Intel® Iris® Xe Graphics — Tiger Lake (`PCI\VEN_8086&DEV_9A49`, HP subsystem `87FE103C`)
- Drivers tested: `31.0.101.5186` (Jan 2024) and `32.0.101.7088` (Jun 2026) — both affected

### Diagnostics Ruled Out
- Hardware-Accelerated GPU Scheduling (HAGS): not enabled
- Hardware Shadow Stack / CET (`UserShadowStack`): NOTSET  
- No third-party AV or EDR (Windows Defender only)
- Fault offset `0x06fefb69` is deterministic across all crash attempts

### Workaround
`--in-process-gpu` flag allows the app to start. `--disable-gpu` alone does **not** fix it (GPU subprocess still crashes).

### Related Issues
- electron/electron#32440 (closed — original report, different exit code `0xC0000005`)
- signalapp/Signal-Desktop#5721 (open — Intel integrated graphics requiring GPU flags)
- signalapp/Signal-Desktop#7828 (open — renderer crash on Windows 11)

nodes.title: Builtin spellchecker never marks text typed into a CodeMirror 6 editor — plain contenteditable works; same page fully checked in plain Chrome 152
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- I have read the Contributing Guidelines for this project.
- I agree to follow the Code of Conduct that this project adheres to.
- I have searched the issue tracker for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

44.0.0

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Ubuntu

### Operating System Version

Ubuntu Linux x64

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

Not bisected

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

No

### Expected Behavior

With the builtin spellchecker enabled (`spellcheck: true` webPreference, `session.setSpellCheckerLanguages(['en-US'])`), any `contenteditable` editing host with `spellcheck="true" lang="en-US"` gets the red squiggle and `context-menu` `params.misspelledWord`/suggestions for misspelled typed text — including one driven by CodeMirror 6.

### Actual Behavior

On a page with three such editables — (1) a plain `contenteditable`, (2) a bare unmodified CodeMirror 6 `EditorView` at top level, (3) the same nested inside another editable — typing `recieve here` into each marks only (1). The CM-driven hosts (2)/(3) are never underlined and the context menu reports no misspelled word.

The marker is never created, as opposed to created-then-wiped: replacing a text node/line **after** typing leaves an existing marker intact. And since only genuinely typed text is marked (attribute toggles / blur-refocus never trigger a re-check), the miss never recovers.

**Why this looks Electron-side, not Blink or CodeMirror:** the identical repro page opened in plain Google Chrome 152.0.7977.82 (Linux, fresh `en-US` profile) spellchecks **all three** boxes, including both CodeMirror editors. The CodeMirror maintainer also could not reproduce on Chromium 152 (Linux): https://discuss.codemirror.net/t/9886. Same Chromium 152 engine, divergent outcomes — the difference is Electron's spellchecker integration.

A plain contenteditable that mimics CM's per-keystroke DOM work (replacing the edited text node or the whole line, re-asserting the selection, synchronously or on rAF) is still checked fine — so it is specifically the live CodeMirror 6 editing host that Electron's after-typing marking pass never services.

### Testcase Gist URL

https://gist.github.com/mauriciolongo/daeff5511fdc9ea402506a917f1a83e5

### Additional Information

The gist is standalone HTML with no application code (unmodified `@codemirror/view` 6.43.1 bundled inline). Load it in a `BrowserWindow` with the builtin spellchecker enabled and type `recieve here` in each box: the plain box squiggles, both CodeMirror boxes stay clean. The same file opened in plain Chrome 152 squiggles all three.

nodes.title: Renderer crashes with CHECK in DidCreateScriptContext after same-process window.open (regression in 42.10.0)
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

42.11.2 (also reproduced on 42.10.0, 42.10.1, 42.11.0, 42.11.1)

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Windows

### Operating System Version

Windows 11 Pro, build 26200

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

42.9.3

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

No

### Expected Behavior

Opening a same-process child window with `window.open('')` from a renderer (contextIsolation: false, sandbox: false) should not crash the renderer.

### Actual Behavior

After the app calls `window.open('', anyName)` (same-process child window; the returned handle can even be discarded), the renderer process crashes silently — exit code `0x80000003` (STATUS_BREAKPOINT), no JS error, no FATAL log line:

- if the child window is **hidden** (`show: false` / 1px off-screen), the renderer dies **~0.5s after the open**, with no further app activity;
- if the child window is **visible**, the renderer stays alive until the **next user interaction** (click / SPA route change) in the opener, then dies.

All same-process windows die together and the app enters a crash-reload loop. 100% reproducible in our production app (8x8 Work — large React SPA); we have not managed to reproduce it in a standalone fiddle despite extensive attempts (details below), which points at a renderer-state-dependent race.

The crash is `CHECK(!environments_.contains(render_frame))` in `ElectronRendererClient::DidCreateScriptContext` (electron_renderer_client.cc:138), reached via lazy `blink::LocalWindowProxy::Initialize` — full symbolicated stacks below. Bisected to 42.10.0; introduced by #53042.

### Testcase Gist URL

https://gist.github.com/riurisniti/a881f20a9cfca62d3e3738d9f13f5c71

### Additional Information

Appologies for the AI generated info dump - not everyday I encouter such esoteric Electron errors so I had to make do.

Note: the gist is a faithful *environment*, not a crashing one - it replays the exact arming step and both detonation choreographies that crash our app 100% of the time, but survives standalone; see the investigation below for why.

### AI Agent result

The regression bisects cleanly to **42.10.0** and is still present in **42.11.2**. 42.9.3 is the last good version. Since #53042 was also backported to 43.x/44.x (#53040), we expect those lines to be affected as well — this currently blocks us from upgrading past 42.9.x on any line.

Renderer configuration: `contextIsolation: false`, `sandbox: false`, `nodeIntegration: false`, preload on the opener window, `webSecurity: false`.

Happy to share minidumps privately and to run instrumented builds / patches against our app, which reproduces this within seconds on every launch.

<details>
<summary>In-depth investigation</summary>

### Symbolicated crash stack

Identical stack shape (same stack-offset layout) in minidumps from **42.11.1** (`electron.exe.pdb` debug id `7097E67EA20201714C4C44205044422E1`, crash at `electron.exe+0x38bcf67`) and **42.11.2** (debug id `37048362CA69C9374C4C44205044422E1`, crash at `electron.exe+0x38d6d67`), symbolicated against symbols.electronjs.org:

```
v8::Object::Get -> v8::internal::Runtime::GetObjectProperty     (a property read)
-> blink::LocalWindowProxy::Initialize()                        (lazy context init)
-> v8::Isolate::InstallConditionalFeatures
-> content::RenderFrameImpl::DidInstallConditionalFeatures
-> electron::ElectronRenderFrameObserver::DidInstallConditionalFeatures (+0xB2 into fn)
-> ElectronRendererClient::DidCreateScriptContext
-> CHECK(!environments_.contains(render_frame))                 (line 138)
```

I.e. a **lazily initialized script context** (created on first property access through a window proxy, not by a navigation — our frame-lifecycle tracing shows zero navigations/frame creations in the ~1.4s before death) hits a RenderFrame that already has an entry in `environments_`.

### Suspected mechanism

#53042 added the per-RenderFrame `environments_` map. `WillReleaseScriptContext` erases an entry only when `env->context() == context`. `window.open('')` gives the child frame an initial-empty-document context (env registered), then commits the real about:blank document in the same RenderFrame. If the first context's release doesn't match the erase condition (or hasn't happened) by the time the committed document's context is **lazily** created on first proxy access, the CHECK fires. The visibility dependence (hidden child → dies in ~0.5s; visible child → dies on next opener interaction) suggests the fatal lazy init is driven by occlusion/backgrounding work in the hidden case and by interaction-driven work in the visible case.

### Reduction results (in our app, each verified by A/B launches)

- **Trigger is fully generic**: one bare `window.open('', name)` suffices. Reproduced with our production window name/features, with a featureless 8-char name, and with a plain non-portal name. Return value discarded.
- **Child preload irrelevant**: crashes both when the child inherits the opener preload and when it is stripped (`webPreferences: { preload: '' }` override — child provably has no preload; browser logs "preload script must have absolute path" and drops it).
- **DevTools ruled out**: crashes with devtools fully disabled (no DevTools webContents exist).
- Our overlay/portal management (hide/setBounds IPC), a meetings iframe subsystem, and everything else app-specific were individually disabled — the crash persists through all of them.
- The crash also reproduces when the `window.open` is **delayed 20s** until the app is fully settled/idle — it is armed by the child window's existence, not by a boot-time race.
- The `0xC0000005` (illegal access) crashes sometimes seen ~0.3s into the post-crash reload appear to be a secondary cascade — possibly the class of bug #53042 aimed to fix.

### Standalone reproduction attempts (all survived)

15+ fiddle/harness scenarios reconstructing the app's conditions: exact webPreferences (contextIsolation:false, sandbox:false, webSecurity:false, preload), file:// and http origins, our full chromium switch set, same-name double-opens and open/close churn, continuous and single-shot delayed property polling of live and stale window handles, iframe srcdoc/data navigation churn, child hide/show/1px choreography with synthetic input events, visible+focused opener, our real ~500KB preload bundle, and app-scale heap replication (~650MB live objects, 8GB --max-old-space-size, GC pressure). None crash. Whatever completes the race appears to be a structural property of a large real-world renderer's heap/object graph.

### Environment notes

- App: 8x8 Work desktop (large React SPA, several same-process `window.open` overlay windows).
- Also reproduced with `--v8-cache-options=none` (ruling out #52988) and with small IPC payloads only (ruling out #53019). 42.11.1's #53329 contextBridge fix did not help.

</details>

Hey @riurisniti Looks like this case did actually crash before aswell (just later in the chain, navigating the child window caused a crash, it now crashes earlier). Should be fixed today. Ty for the report
Thanks @MarshallOfSound for the prompt fix! I'll test it out as soon as a new patch is released

nodes.title: Normal interface text renders as monospace in Electron apps on KDE Wayland
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist
- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version
40.10.2

### What operating system(s) are you using?
Other Linux

### Operating System Version
Aurora DX NVIDIA Open stable image 44.20260901.1, KDE Plasma 6.7.4 on Wayland, kernel 7.1.6-201.fc44.x86_64

### What arch are you using?
x64

### Last Known Working Electron version
_No response_

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?
I don't know how to test

### Expected Behavior
Normal interface text should render using the requested proportional UI font family, such as Noto Sans, while semantic code and terminal text remain monospaced.

### Actual Behavior
In Hermes Desktop (Electron 40.10.2) and Grok Bot, normal interface text renders as a monospace font even though KDE and fontconfig resolve the requested UI families correctly.

### Testcase Gist URL
_No response_

### Additional Information
The behavior is reproducible on the currently booted `aurora-dx-nvidia-open:stable` image.

<details><summary>In-depth investigation</summary>

The same host-level Electron/Chromium font-matching behavior also affects unrelated Electron applications, while an embedded webfont bypasses it.

Changing the Hermes CSS stack to put `system-ui` first, with an explicit `Noto Sans` fallback, did not change the physical font. The reliable workaround was to bundle Noto Sans Regular/Medium/Bold as application webfonts under a private family name and put that family first. After rebuilding, proportional UI text rendered correctly while semantic code and terminal text remained monospaced.

Relevant font resolution output:

```
KDE general font: Noto Sans 10
fc-match system-ui: Noto Sans Regular
fc-match sans-serif: Noto Sans Regular
fc-match "Noto Sans": Noto Sans Regular
```

The issue was reproduced in Hermes Desktop and Grok Bot, and appears unlikely to be VS Code-specific. Package versions remain `fontconfig-2.17.0-4.fc44`, `freetype-2.14.3-1.fc44`, and `harfbuzz-14.1.0-2.fc44`.

</details>

<!-- end-of-life -->

Hello @viniciosrab. Thanks for reporting this and helping to make Electron better!

The version of Electron reported in this issue has reached end-of-life and is [no longer supported](https://www.electronjs.org/docs/latest/tutorial/electron-timelines#timeline). If you're still experiencing this issue on a [supported version](https://releases.electronjs.org/) of Electron, please update this issue to reflect that version of Electron.

Now adding the https://github.com/electron/electron/labels/blocked%2Fneed-info%20%E2%9D%8C label for this reason. This issue will be closed in 10 days if the above is not addressed.

Related report from Aurora: [ublue-os/aurora#2680](https://github.com/ublue-os/aurora/issues/2680#issuecomment-5535583026)

The linked comment contains additional reproduction details for the same Electron font-rendering behavior on Aurora Linux.

I think this is your GTK font setting, not fontconfig.

`system-ui` in Chromium on Linux comes from GTK's `gtk-font-name`, so `fc-match system-ui` doesn't tell us anything here (fontconfig doesn't know `system-ui` and just gives you the default sans font). On Wayland, GTK reads that setting from the GNOME GSettings key `org.gnome.desktop.interface font-name`, not from the KDE font settings. So KDE can say Noto Sans while GTK, and therefore Electron, hands out a monospace font.

I reproduced this on Electron 40.10.2 under a headless Wayland compositor with the Fedora 44 font packages. With KDE's `settings.ini` set to `Noto Sans,  10` and that GSettings key set to a monospace font, `system-ui, 'Noto Sans', sans-serif` renders monospace and plain `sans-serif` is fine. That matches what you saw when you put `system-ui` first.

Can you check what it's set to?

```
gsettings get org.gnome.desktop.interface font-name
```

If that's a monospace font, this should fix it:

```
gsettings set org.gnome.desktop.interface font-name 'Noto Sans 10'
```

Launching one of the apps with `--ozone-platform=x11` should also render correctly, because GTK then reads KDE's settings through XSettings. If the apps are Flatpaks the value comes from the settings portal instead, so let us know if that's the case.
Closing this out as the info we requested hasn't been provided

nodes.title: [Bug] Native addons deriving from `node::ObjectWrap` abort during GC on Node 24.19.0 / 24.20.0
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

42.11.0

### What operating system(s) are you using?

macOS

### Operating System Version

macOS 26.3.1 

### What arch are you using?

arm64 (including Apple Silicon)

### Last Known Working Electron version

42.10.0

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

I don't know how to test

### Expected Behavior

A native addon deriving from `node::ObjectWrap` should not abort the process when its wrapped JS object is garbage collected.

### Actual Behavior

After upgrading to 42.11.0 the main process aborts with SIGABRT from inside a V8 first-pass weak callback. The crash happens on a `worker_threads` thread of the main process. Symbolized frames from the minidump:

```
libsystem_kernel      __pthread_kill
libsystem_c           abort
Electron Framework    node::Assert(node::AssertionInfo const&)                        node_errors.cc
Electron Framework    node::RemoveEnvironmentCleanupHook(v8::Isolate*, void (*)(void*), void*) + 220
better_sqlite3.node   Statement::~Statement() + 312
better_sqlite3.node   Statement::~Statement() + 12
Electron Framework    v8::internal::GlobalHandles::InvokeFirstPassWeakCallbacks()
Electron Framework    v8::internal::Heap::CollectGarbage(...)
Electron Framework    v8::internal::HeapAllocator::CollectGarbageAndRetryAllocation(...)
Electron Framework    v8::internal::HeapAllocator::AllocateRawSlowPath(...)
Electron Framework    v8::internal::Runtime_AllocateInYoungGeneration(...)
                      [JS frames]
Electron Framework    node::worker::MessagePort::OnMessage(...)
Electron Framework    node::worker::Worker::StartThread(...)
```

The addon is a fork of better-sqlite3; its `Statement` class derives from `node::ObjectWrap`. The destructor itself contains no Node API calls — the call to `RemoveEnvironmentCleanupHook` comes from the inlined `node::ObjectWrap::~ObjectWrap()`.

We have not captured the process stderr, so we do not have the printed assertion text. In Node v24.19.0 the only CHECK in `RemoveEnvironmentCleanupHook` is `CHECK_NOT_NULL(env)` at `src/api/hooks.cc:142`.

**Root cause**

42.11.0 updated Node.js to v24.19.0 (#52634).

v24.19.0 backported nodejs/node#63642 (`4b5eb7b72d`, "src: add cleanup hooks to `node::ObjectWrap`"), which makes the `node::ObjectWrap` constructor and destructor call `AddEnvironmentCleanupHook` / `RemoveEnvironmentCleanupHook`. `ObjectWrap` is header-only, so this call is compiled into any addon built against these headers.

v24.19.0 does not include nodejs/node#63985 (`1723773d41`, "src: keep global list of addon-provided cleanup hooks"), which reworks `RemoveEnvironmentCleanupHook` to resolve the hook through a global registry instead of the current `Environment`. From that commit message:

> This occasionally breaks down when `RemoveEnvironmentCleanupHook()` is called during garbage collection -- which would be an expected use case of the functionality, but one that has not been covered through our tests before 215027c8eded2e.

In v24.19.0 and v24.20.0, `src/api/hooks.cc` still has:

```cpp
void RemoveEnvironmentCleanupHook(Isolate* isolate,
                                  CleanupHook fun,
                                  void* arg) {
  Environment* env = Environment::GetCurrent(isolate);
  CHECK_NOT_NULL(env);
  env->RemoveCleanupHook(fun, arg);
}
```

and `Environment::GetCurrent(v8::Isolate*)` in `src/env-inl.h` returns `nullptr` when `isolate->InContext()` is false, which is the case while V8 invokes first-pass weak callbacks.

**Affected branches**

Both Node v24.19.0 and v24.20.0 versions contain #63642 without #63985.

**Upstream status (checked 2026-09-02)**

- nodejs/node#65042, the `[v24.x backport]` of #63985, is open and labelled `blocked`. Last activity 2026-08-13.
- It is blocked on nodejs/node#65195 / #65630, a use-after-free in `CleanupHookThunkRun` arising from the interaction of #63642 and #63985. #65630 is still open.
- nodejs/node#65446 tracks the 24.19.0 side of this.

So #63985 does not appear to be independently applicable: nodejs/node#65195 reports that it is what introduces the use-after-free that #65630 fixes.

### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_

### Additional Information

Filing this for visibility. Whether and how to address it before Node ships a fixed v24.x is entirely up to the Electron maintainers.

The crashing class derives from `node::ObjectWrap`, so the trigger is the `ObjectWrap` destructor path rather than anything specific to this addon — any addon rebuilt against 24.19.0+ headers should be affected.
